classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the perpendicular bisects the 16 m chord, then use the explicitly requested Pythagoras method with half the chord and the radius.

content.prompt: Find the length $OM$. Use Pythagoras’ Theorem.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, radii OA and OB, chord AB, and perpendicular OM. An external dimension line labels the whole chord AB.
spec.mathematics: OB = 10 m; AB = 16 m; OM is perpendicular to AB. M is the midpoint of AB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the length OM is not supplied.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so $MB=8\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned}OM^2&=OB^2-MB^2\\OM^2&=10^2-8^2\\OM^2&=36\\OM&=6\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
